 Prediction pivot: Robinhood ( HOOD ) slides on report of KALSHI eyeing stock trading .

 Unions mobilize: France braces for more protests amid calls for nationwide strike .

 Delivery scrutiny: DOJ to review DoorDash's ( DASH ) $17B deal to buy Instacart ( CART ).
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 Critical test 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
 The loss of one of the leaders of the AI revolution, Jensen Huang of Nvidia ( NVDA ), continues to reverberate across the investing world. High-profile names ranging from Tesla's ( TSLA ) Elon Musk to Shopify's ( SHOP ) Tobias Lütke have called for him to be reinstated, as well as advocacy in the world of politics, like backing from President Trump. Efforts to bring him back are now taking place inside Nvidia amid a groundswell of support from employees and senior staff.

 Snapshot: A letter seen by The Wall Street Journal revealed that Nader Khalil, director of developer technology at Nvidia, sent a new warning to top brass and the company's board of directors. "Irreplaceable talent at Nvidia is now contemplating departing," he wrote, adding that Jensen Huang's "global relationships are a strategic advantage for this company" and "his leadership is critical to maintain American dominance in AI." More than 188,000 people have also reportedly signed a petition demanding the return of Huang, while prominent Nvidia shareholders like Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management have urged the company not to rush a replacement before all the facts are known.

Historic notable comebacks, however, like the ones seen by tech leaders Sam Altman in 2023 and Steve Jobs in 1997, took place under very different circumstances. Neither left over personal misconduct nor national security threats, and OpenAI was a private company insulated from public shareholder lawsuits. Huang's case involves significant HR violations surrounding subordinate affairs, as well as a relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset that has triggered a federal probe into AI chip exports. Nvidia: Jensen Huang Could Return As CEO 

 Outlook: This is all taking place as Nvidia ( NVDA ) this afternoon hosts its first earnings call in 33 years without Jensen Huang at the head. Interim chief executive Colette Kress, who also remains CFO, will seek to assure shareholders about sales growth guidance and the innovation engine at Nvidia, as well as potential risks from the tightening of export restrictions . Nvidia has already lost over $2 trillion in market capitalization over the past six weeks, and has declined 16% so far this year, compared to the 8% rise of the broader S&P 500 Index. What will Nvidia say on the earnings call? ( 5 comments )
